title: A task's gate is measured once and runs what the task can break
description: A paired measurement put the plugin near four times a plain session's wall time per task, with the task gate carrying almost all of the difference and the writer none of it. More than half of the gate time was a second full measurement of a tree the first run had just called green: the drive reads a background gate back by asking the recorded gate again, and that ask is refused a repeat whenever any entry names the plan, an evidence file or a journal file, or merely a test file whose name contains one of those words. Beyond the repeat, a task's recorded gate runs entries the project's own configuration says belong to the phase gate, tasks minted before a subset spelling was recorded keep the whole phase gate, and the declared suites and the affected suites run as two calls one after the other. Entry: the stage record of the previous phase is on main, so each change here is read from a task's own timing rather than from a ledger query. Exit: replaying the recorded gate of the measured tasks on the phase's head shows no second measurement of a tree-grading step, and the per-task gate time printed by status is at or under a third of what it was on the same tasks.
desiredOutcome: A green task gate is not measured a second time when nothing it graded has changed, an entry the project leaves to the phase gate is not run by a task's recorded gate, a task whose wide gate was stored before the project recorded how to run a subset gets the narrow one, and the suites a task declares and the suites its change can break run as one call. On the recorded pairs the task gate's share of the gap to a plain session falls to what one narrow run costs.

tasks.title: A recorded gate repeats the steps that grade the tree and measures again only the steps that grade the plan
tasks.description: Today one entry that names a left-out path makes the whole run measured again, so a gate holding the manifest validator beside a sweep and a browser check pays for all three twice. Decide the repeat per step. A step that names no left-out path repeats from the newest measured row with the same identity, exactly as a whole run does now; a step that names one is run again, because what it reads (the plan) is not in the identity and may have moved. The row such a run writes says, step by step, which were repeated and from which run and which were measured, and its verdict is the worst of the two kinds. When every step repeats the run prints the existing reuse banner unchanged; when some were measured it prints a line of its own naming them and their seconds, and the row's verdictSource says so with a third word rather than reusing either existing one. The statuses that may be repeated stay the ones allowed today, a muted row is still not a source, and --no-reuse still measures everything. A red run repeats as red: the statuses that may be repeated already include failed, and that matters, because the drive reads a background run back by asking again, and a second measurement that comes out green replaces a red verdict nobody was shown (seen on this repository: one task's background run failed on one case and the read-back's own run on the same identity passed, and the task closed green). Dependants you answer for: _evidence_io.reusable_run and its callers; _verdict_binding and stamp-verification, which bind a commit and a stamp to a run and must accept a row whose steps are part repeated; the drive's stored_green and verdict_basis; gate_mean_ms and the gate budget, which must not count a repeated step's old duration as time spent now; audit-usage's reused-against-measured comparison; the report's and the panel's rendering of a reused row, which read verdictSource and must show an unknown word as itself; verify-invariants; COMPATIBILITY.md's list of evidence row keys and verdictSource words. Acceptance: (1) a gate of one tree-grading step and one plan-grading step, asked twice with no change, runs the tree step once and the plan step twice, and the second row names the first run as the source of the repeated step; (2) the same gate after an edit to a declared file measures both steps; (3) the same gate after the manifest alone changed in a way that turns the plan step red records a red verdict, with the tree step repeated; (4) a gate with no plan-grading step behaves byte for byte as before; (5) --no-reuse measures every step; (6) a repeated step's duration is not added to the time the row says the run took; (7) a red run asked again with no change repeats as red, with no second measurement of its tree-grading steps; (8) a commit is bound and a stamp verified against a part-repeated row exactly as against a measured one.

tasks.title: The drive reads a background gate's own verdict back, says what was measured again and why, and its fixtures drive a gate that grades the plan
tasks.description: The drive reads a background gate back by asking the recorded gate again, and prints that the run did not repeat on this tree whenever the reuse banner is missing, whatever the reason; its comments say a second ask on the same content measures nothing, which was false for every gate holding a plan-grading entry. The same happens to the phase gate at sign-off, which was measured whole a second time. Worse than the time, a read-back that measures again can replace the verdict the drive handed out: a background run that came back red was followed by a green second run on the same identity, and the task closed with the red never shown. The verdict of the run the drive launched is the one it acts on: a red background run goes to the base measurement and the decision exactly as an inline red does, for a task gate and for the phase gate alike. With repeats decided per step, the read-back line names what was repeated and what was measured again, with the measured steps' names and seconds, and says did not repeat only when a tree-grading step was measured again, with the reason the gate printed. The comments state what the code now does. The drive's gate fixtures use true and false as the gate, so the drive never met a plan-grading entry: add fixtures whose gate holds one. Dependants you answer for: the decision table and every step text in tests/test_drive_phase.py; the cases that require exactly one task-gate call carrying the reuse banner after a background run; the prompt hook and the orchestrator, which read the signal line and the did lines; the stage record the previous phase added, where a read-back that measured steps is a gate stage of its own with its real length and a fully repeated one adds none.
